transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 09:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Ethan Walker, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Liam Chen, Rita Alvarez, Marcus Holt, Ana Duarte (CumulusWorks)

Auto-summary (auto): quick alignment on adapter benchmark plan, KMS compatibility, and marketplace packaging checklist. Agreed to run a latency pilot and exchange a bench spreadsheet + runbook links.

Topics:
- Marketplace adapter certification requirements
- KMS integration and encryption in transit/at rest
- Latency/cost benchmarks for quantized model variants
- Networking: VPC peering, CIDR, egress costs
- Packaging: Helm/OCI image + listing artifacts

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account. We got Ethan and Priya from product engineering on the call, super excited to sync.
[00:18] Liam Chen: Hey Sofia, Liam here. We're hoping to nail down what "certification" means for CumulusWorks marketplace and get a bench plan so we can sign off with our compliance folks.
[00:32] Ethan Walker: Cool, quick context — Redwood's adapter is what we'd call the marketplace connector that lives in your VPC or as a hybrid agent depending on your listing. It supports Dedicated, Hosted fallback, and our Private deploy patterns. Sorry sometimes the naming gets a bit messy in the docs, you might see "Redwood Dedicade" or "Redwood Private plane" in older notes.
[00:50] Rita Alvarez: Yeah, security is the main ask. We need KMS/HSM compatibility, audit logs, and proof that customer data never leaves our network unless explicitly allowed.
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Totally. On KMS we support bring-your-own-key patterns — works with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and some HSM flows. For the marketplace listing we usually ask for a test key in staging so we can run a "verification job" and show the audit entries in the console.
[01:22] Marcus Holt: When you say "verification job" what does that actually look like? Are you running tokenized requests, or full inference? Concerned about egress costs.
[01:38] Ethan Walker: Good question. We do a mix — first we run small synthetic traffic to validate crypto and end-to-end connectivity. Then we run a latency bench that mirrors your real traffic profile (prompt length, concurrency). For the lat bench we can run both prefix cache warmed and cold starts so you can see real-world tail latencies.
[01:58] Ana Duarte: Do you require us to open ports or install operators? Our infra team prefers minimal footprint.
[02:10] Sofia Martinez: We have two packaging options: a Helm chart that deploys a lightweight connector + sidecar, or an OCI image you can run as a single container with a service account. The Helm path requires Helm v3 and some RBAC setup; the image path needs less infra work but you'll need to hand us a service account with KMS decrypt rights in staging for the test.
[02:35] Liam Chen: Ok. From a go-to-market perspective we also need the listing artifact — icons, short/long descriptions, pricing tiers. But one step at a time, let's get the technical sign-off first.
[02:48] [crosstalk]
[02:50] Rita Alvarez: Quick note — our security reviewer called out that audit logs must include token-level hashes, not raw payloads. Is that in your current logging?
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: We redact PII by default in hosted but when running in your VPC the logs are under your control. We emit audit events with HMAC'd token ids; sometimes the transcript tooling shows raw prompt snippets in debug mode but we don't retain debug traces in production. We'll share a sample of the audit format after this call.
[03:28] Marcus Holt: Networking — for peering we need to know expected ports and IP ranges. Also curious about cross-account peering cost impact.
[03:43] Ethan Walker: For the connector we use HTTPS outbound to our control plane for orchestration but inference traffic stays local to the GPU nodes in your VPC for private deploys. For marketplace deployments: if you're listing in the public marketplace but using a private connector, traffic remains in your VPC; only control plane signals go out (keepalive, healthchecks). We'll send the exact CIDR list but typically it's a handful of egress IPs.
[04:05] [00:04:05] Sofia Martinez: We should flag that if you choose Dedicated capacity via Redwood, there is an SLA and more persistent egress to Redwood's regional endpoints — something your billing team will want to see.
[04:22] Liam Chen: Let's talk benchmarks. We run a lot of multi-turn chat, median prompt length ~110 tokens, 8 concurrent workers. What do you need from us to model that?
[04:36] Ethan Walker: We'll need a sample prompt set (anonymized), expected concurrency, cold vs warm start ratio, and target p95 latency SLO. For our initial bench we'll use a quantized 13B model variant (int8/4) to give you a realistic cost/latency sweet spot.
[04:54] Rita Alvarez: Is quantization safe from a quality/regression perspective? Our product team is picky.
[05:06] Priya Kapoor: We run evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload and gives a delta report comparing output similarity metrics. We can publish BLEU/ROUGE-style diffs and human-captured quality checks. For CumulusWorks we can tag any model variant clearly in the listing UI so customers know which flavor they're using.
[05:30] Marcus Holt: Can we see an example of the benchmark spreadsheet?
[05:36] Ethan Walker: Yes — I'll send our bench spreadsheet after this call. It includes columns for model variant, instance type, batch size, tokens/sec, p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens estimated.
[05:49] Ana Duarte: On the KMS path: our default is GCP KMS with a centralized key policy. If you need an HSM we can request one but that adds procurement.
[06:02] Priya Kapoor: GCP KMS is supported. For HSM-backed keys we have a few extra steps around attestation and key wrapping. If you can provision a staging key we can validate the decrypt flow and show the KMS audit log entries.
[06:15] [00:06:15] Sofia Martinez: Action item check — Ethan will produce preliminary latency numbers for a quantized 13B and the bench spreadsheet; Rita will provision a staging KMS key; Sofia will share marketplace packaging checklist.
[06:29] Liam Chen: Perfect. Also, shelf life — how long do you keep benchmark artifacts? We need them retained for our security audit.
[06:40] Ethan Walker: We can export bench runs and logs to your storage (S3/GCS) and set retention policies. We don't keep raw prompts unless you ask us to. For audits we provide a certified run artifact with hashes and the audit log.
[06:57] Rita Alvarez: About the listing itself — are there any friction points in your marketplace review? e.g., custom network integrations that delay publication?
[07:10] Priya Kapoor: Occasionally, yes. Marketplace gate checks include packaging format (Helm or OCI), schema for pricing, a short security questionnaire, and a connectivity test. If the connector needs special cross-account roles or long-lived keys that can slow review — we prefer ephemeral credentials for testing.
[07:29] Marcus Holt: Ephemeral creds — can you support Workload Identity or OIDC?
[07:35] Ethan Walker: We support OIDC and Workload Identity for GKE, plus federated roles for AWS. It's in our doc but we can add a snippet to the checklist specific to your infra.
[07:49] [00:07:49] Ana Duarte: For the UI listing—pricing tiering: do you have metering hooks for per-invocation billing vs subscription? We need both.
[07:59] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Redwood supports per-token metering and fixed subscription tiers. For marketplace we can surface both pricing flavors; the connector will report token usage to your billing exporter or to Redwood depending on the model you choose.
[08:18] Liam Chen: Let's lock on timeline. We want listing QA completed by late July. Is that feasible?
[08:26] Priya Kapoor: If we get the staging KMS key and staging VPC next week, we can run the bench and sign the technical cert within two weeks, so late July is reasonable.
[08:37] Rita Alvarez: One more security nit — RBAC in the console. Our auditors want granular role separation: listing manager vs operator vs billing viewer.
[08:49] Priya Kapoor: We support SAML/SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. We'll send the RBAC schema; you can map to your groups.
[08:59] Ethan Walker: Quick technical note on quantization: if you go int8 with our recommended kernels you should see 30-45% cost reduction and ~10-20% latency improvement on p50; p95 gains depend on batch shaping and KV cache hit rates. We'll include these expected deltas in the bench spreadsheet.
[09:22] Marcus Holt: For private deployments, what telemetry do you push back to Redwood control plane? We need to be explicit for compliance.
[09:33] Priya Kapoor: Minimal telemetry: health, node metrics, and anonymized usage aggregates (no raw prompts). Everything is opt-in — we can run in fully air-gapped mode for on-prem where the control plane does not receive metrics.
[09:46] Sofia Martinez: ok let's go over deliverables and owners quickly.
[09:50] [00:09:50] Sofia Martinez: Deliverables: bench spreadsheet + runbook (Ethan), KMS staging key (Rita), staging VPC + peering config (Marcus), marketplace packaging checklist + RBAC schema (Sofia). We'll also schedule the 2-hr latency pilot during the week of 6/22.
[10:12] Liam Chen: Sounds good. Please make the bench run include a cold start sweep and a warm cache sweep. The cold path is critical for our UX team.
[10:23] Ethan Walker: Noted — cold and warm, and we'll include sample tail-percentile traces.
[10:29] Ana Duarte: Can we also include a sample human-eval snapshot? Just 10 hand-eval prompts to eyeball quality.
[10:36] Priya Kapoor: Yes — we'll provide a small eval set and suggested acceptance thresholds. You can sign off or request rollback to a full-precision variant.
[10:47] Rita Alvarez: On legal — we'll need a data handling addendum. Who should we route that to?
[10:54] Sofia Martinez: Send it to legal@redwood.ai and cc me; I'll loop in our contracts lead. We'll attach the standard marketplace DPA and SOC report.
[11:05] [00:11:05] Closing notes/crosstalk
[11:08] Liam Chen: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. Looking forward to the bench.
[11:12] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and links. Meeting adjourned.
